Effects of Estrogen: The development of the ovarian follicles increases the level of estrogen. It rebuilds the endometrium, preparing the uterus for fertilization. The increasing level of estrogen also produces a negative feedback on the brain, causing it to make less follicular stimulating hormone, or FSH and luteinizing hormone, LH, ovarian follicles stop their development, and one becomes dominant. Later in this phase, the high level of estrogen switches the feedback from negative to positive, causing a surge of LH necessary for ovulation.
Effects of Progesterone: The level of progesterone stays low throughout the follicular phase.
Effects of FSH: The level of the Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH) decreases because of the negative feedback from estrogen. The development of follicles slows down, and one follicle becomes dominant.
Effects of LH: The rising level of estrogen produces a negative feedback on the brain, keeping the Luteinizing Hormone (LH) secretion relatively low.
Energy Levels Info: You might start feeling more refreshed and physically stronger. Training will feel easier and muscle recovery will feel quicker. Now you can start increasing your exercise intensity.
What to eat: Eat foods that will boost your energy levels. Some example of great foods for your follicular phase include fresh fruits, vegetables such as spinach, nuts and seeds, whole grains, lean proteins such as chicken and fish, and healthy fats.
Foods and Recipes: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration: At this stage your brain has the lowest level of dynamical complexity, making it be less networked. Due to this, you might feel slower and foggier. Some tips to manage concentrating during this time is to alter diet for brain healthy foods, schedule your time and work strategically so you can still meet your expectations.
Health: The length for the follicular phase can vary, which will ultimately alter the menstrual cycle length. The average total cycle length for individuals are 28 days, however if your cycle is greater than 35 days or shorter than 21 days it is recommended that you visit your doctor as that can be a sign of oligomenorrhea and polymenorrhea.
Mood: Throughout the follicular phase your mood levels will increase due to the increase in serotonin. You might feel more optimistic, social and have a positive outlook.
Types of Vitamins: Some Vitamins and supplements that you can take throughout your follicular phase consist of Vitamin B to support your energy levels, Omega 3 for heart, brain health, and zinc to help with hormonal balance and contribute to normal fertility.  Before taking any supplements, please contact your doctor.
Insights in the Brain: The rising level of estrogen produces a negative feedback on the hypothalamus / anterior pituitary system that decreases the production of FSH and LH.
Insights in the Ovaries: Multiple ovarian follicles are developing under Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH) influence.
Insights in the Uterus: The uterus is in proliferative state: the increasing level of estrogen thickens the endometrium, the functional layer is regenerated and cervical mucus becomes thinner and more elastic. It prepares the uterus for a possible implantation.
Phase Info: One of the multiple ovarian follicles becomes dominant. The uterus prepares for a possible implantation.
Today's Recap: Today you may feel more refreshed and stronger. You might feel foggier but have a more positive outlook.

Insights in the Brain: The level of estrogen is high enough to switch the feedback from a negative to a positive one, increasing the production of LH surge.
Insights in the Ovaries: One ovarian follicle becomes dominant, and the others regress. This dominant follicle produces a high amount of estrogens.
Insights in the Uterus: The uterus is in proliferative state: the increasing level of estrogen thickens the endometrium, the functional layer is regenerated and cervical mucus becomes thinner and more elastic. It prepares the uterus for a possible implantation.
Phase Info: One of the multiple ovarian follicles becomes dominant. The uterus prepares for a possible implantation.
Today's Recap: Today you may feel more refreshed and stronger. You might feel foggier but have a more positive outlook.

Effects of Estrogen: The development of the ovarian follicles increases the level of estrogen. It rebuilds the endometrium, preparing the uterus for fertilization. The increasing level of estrogen also produces a negative feedback on the brain, causing it to make less follicular stimulating hormone, or FSH and luteinizing hormone, LH, ovarian follicles stop their development, and one becomes dominant. Later in this phase, the high level of estrogen switches the feedback from negative to positive, causing a surge of LH necessary for ovulation.
Effects of Progesterone: The level of progesterone stays low throughout the follicular phase.
Effects of FSH: The level of the Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH) decreases because of the negative feedback from estrogen. The development of follicles slows down, and one follicle becomes dominant.
Effects of LH: The rising level of estrogen produces a negative feedback on the brain, keeping the Luteinizing Hormone (LH) secretion relatively low.
Energy Levels Info: You are entering the late follicular phase and therefore you might feel more refreshed and physically stronger. Now is the perfect time for high intensity workouts.
What to eat: Eat foods that will boost your energy levels. Ensure that your diet is balanced to support hormonal balance and egg maturation in preparation for ovulation. An example of these foods include vegetables, fruits, chicken, and whole grains
Foods and Recipes: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration: In the late follicular phase you will be feeling at your best performance, this is due to the brain being the most dynamic state, resulting in you feeling energized, sharp and confident. Your memory and attention span will be at peak performance.
Health: The length for the follicular phase can vary, which will ultimately alter the menstrual cycle length. The average total cycle length for individuals are 28 days, however if your cycle is greater than 35 days or shorter than 21 days it is recommended that you visit your doctor as that can be a sign of oligomenorrhea and polymenorrhea.
Mood: Throughout the follicular phase your mood levels will increase due to the increase in serotonin. You might feel more optimistic, social and have a positive outlook.
